title: Import Pasilla gene counts and test the RNAi treatment effect

sources.locator: Count matrix input; chunks loadPasilla, reorderPasila, matrixInput, deseq; About the pasilla dataset
bundled extdata count matrix path and tree size (167602 bytes)
bundled extdata sample annotation path and tree size (527 bytes)
package description and linked GEO accessions; retrieved 2026-09-30

scientific_use: Align the sample annotation to columns in a gene-by-sample count matrix, construct a DESeqDataSet with condition design, fit the negative-binomial model, and extract condition log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values for Pasilla RNAi knockdown versus untreated samples.
tool_role_basis: The vignette composes DESeq2 public constructors, DESeq, and results on an existing count matrix; it does not implement the underlying statistical algorithm.
inputs: Bundled gzip TSV gene-count matrix and CSV sample annotations; counts are unnormalized integer reads, rows are genes and columns are samples.
Sample metadata include condition and sequencing type; annotation row IDs require removal of the fb prefix and reordering to match count-matrix columns.
A condition design (~ condition) is used in this specific standard workflow; the adjacent multifactor workflow adds sequencing type.
outputs: DESeqDataSet with fitted size factors, dispersions, and model coefficients.
DESeqResults table with baseMean, log2FoldChange, standard error, Wald statistic, p-value, and adjusted p-value; default results apply Cook's-distance flagging and independent filtering.
dependencies: R and DESeq2 with its Bioconductor dependencies, including SummarizedExperiment and S4Vectors.
Input sample order must be reconciled explicitly; DESeq2 does not infer matching between matrix columns and metadata rows.
evidence: Vignette Count matrix input and chunks loadPasilla/reorderPasila/matrixInput/deseq describe exact read paths, alignment, construction, fitting and result extraction.
Vignette About the pasilla dataset identifies Drosophila melanogaster cell cultures and RNAi knockdown of pasilla.
Official Bioconductor pasilla page reports per-gene/per-exon counts and GEO GSM461176-GSM461181; this is package-level context, not proof that every accession is present in the bundled subset.
limitations: The bundled count file itself was not downloaded or opened; tree metadata reports its path and compressed size only.
No analysis was executed. Confirm the desired gene universe and exact count/annotation release during authoring.
Package source license does not by itself settle redistribution terms for the observations; check the data package and source study terms before release.

title: Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport

sources.locator: Transcript abundance files and tximport / tximeta; chunks txiSetup, txiFiles, tximport, txi2dds
tximportData package vignette describes sample output files from GEUVADIS; retrieved 2026-09-30

scientific_use: Import Salmon quant.sf files for six samples, aggregate transcript-level abundance to gene-level estimates using a transcript-to-gene table, and construct a DESeqDataSet while preserving estimated-count and transcript-length offset information for differential analysis.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow invokes tximport and DESeq2 constructors to apply existing quantification-import and differential-analysis tools.
inputs: Sample table with run IDs and condition metadata; six gzipped Salmon quant.sf files under tximportData extdata; tx2gene.gencode.v27.csv transcript-to-gene mapping.
The vignette makes two demonstration condition labels and notes real analyses should use the actual sample table.
outputs: tximport result containing gene-level estimated counts and abundance/length information.
DESeqDataSet created with design ~ condition and suitable as the input to the standard DESeq2 analysis.
dependencies: R, DESeq2, tximport, readr, tximportData, Salmon-produced quant.sf files and compatible transcript-to-gene mapping.
evidence: Pinned vignette specifies input file patterns, tx2gene mapping, tximport(files,type="salmon",tx2gene=tx2gene), and DESeqDataSetFromTximport.
Official tximportData vignette identifies these package files as quantifier outputs for six GEUVADIS samples.
limitations: DESeq2 repository does not contain these external quantification files; full sample identity, exact package release and terms need confirmation.
No quantification or differential analysis was executed; transcript-to-gene mapping compatibility and salmon index provenance remain authoring decisions.

title: Estimate treatment effects while adjusting for sequencing type

sources.locator: Multi-factor designs; chunks multifactor, copyMultifactor, fixLevels, replaceDesign, multiResults, multiTypeResults
chunk runPasilla; test-suite fit design ~ type + condition and relevel untreated

scientific_use: Refit Pasilla counts using a fixed-effects design that accounts for sequencing type while estimating the treatment effect, then extract either the treatment contrast or sequencing-type contrast.
tool_role_basis: This is a documented application of DESeq2 design formulas, DESeq, and results to an observed count dataset; no underlying tool algorithm is implemented.
inputs: Pasilla gene counts and matching condition/type metadata, with factor levels cleaned and the untreated condition as reference.
Design formula ~ type + condition; the vignette positions condition last so default results report that effect.
outputs: Fitted DESeqDataSet and DESeqResults for treatment effect adjusted for sequencing type.
Optional results contrast for single versus paired sequencing type.
dependencies: DESeq2 and Bioconductor object dependencies; full-rank design and correctly aligned metadata are required.
evidence: Vignette states condition is biological interest and type indicates sequencing protocol, then fits ~ type + condition and extracts results.
Test-suite runPasilla independently constructs the same design and relevels condition to untreated.
limitations: The cited sources do not provide a task-specific expected result table or grading contract.
Assess design rank and factor-level semantics from the selected exact metadata during authoring; no execution was performed.

title: Transform counts and assess sample-level structure with PCA and distances

sources.locator: Blind dispersion estimation through Principal component plot sections; chunks rlogAndVST, sampleClust, figHeatmapSamples, figPCA, figPCA2

scientific_use: Apply variance-stabilizing or regularized-log transformations for exploratory quality assessment, then inspect sample-to-sample distances, heatmaps and PCA grouped by condition and sequencing type.
tool_role_basis: The source applies existing DESeq2 transformations and visualization functions to count data; the task is exploratory analysis rather than implementation of those methods.
inputs: DESeqDataSet with raw counts, sample metadata and a design; vignette uses Pasilla dds.
Transformation blind parameter controls whether sample design is ignored for QA; vst can use prior dispersion estimates with blind=FALSE.
outputs: DESeqTransform with normalized transformed assay values.
Sample distance matrix/heatmap and PCA coordinates or plot with percent variance explained.
dependencies: DESeq2, R plotting dependencies (ggplot2; pheatmap and RColorBrewer for examples); optional vsn package for meanSdPlot.
evidence: Vignette describes blind dispersion estimation for unbiased sample QA and shows vst(dds,blind=FALSE), dist(t(assay(vsd))), pheatmap and plotPCA.
vst manual says the wrapper deterministically subsets genes spanning mean normalized-count range to estimate the dispersion trend.
limitations: The source gives plots and exploratory outputs but no objective sample-removal rule or expected clustering labels.
A plot-level task needs a defined artifact and evaluation protocol; no graphics were generated here.

title: Test multiple design terms with a likelihood-ratio test

sources.locator: Time-series experiments; Likelihood ratio test; chunks simpleLRT and simpleLRT2
chunk runFission and plotFission: design ~ strain + minute + strain:minute; reduced ~ strain + minute

scientific_use: Compare full and reduced negative-binomial GLMs to test whether an interaction or other set of design terms improves fit; the fission example tests strain-by-time interaction and plots counts for a selected gene over time by strain.
tool_role_basis: DESeq2's existing DESeq(test="LRT") and results APIs perform the inference; the sources compose them for time-course and interaction analyses.
inputs: Count data and metadata for samples; full design and nested reduced design that removes the terms being tested.
The test-suite example uses fission data with strain and minute and compares ~ strain + minute + strain:minute against ~ strain + minute.
outputs: DESeqResults whose p-values/statistic reflect the joint deviance difference for removed terms; the displayed log2 fold change is one coefficient and does not alone summarize the multi-term test.
Example plotCounts data/plot for the smallest-p-value gene over minute, grouped by strain.
dependencies: DESeq2 and fission Bioconductor data package for the concrete example; sample design must support estimable full/reduced models.
evidence: Vignette explains LRT as full-versus-reduced likelihood/deviance comparison and documents reduced-model specification.
Test-suite runFission specifies interaction design and reduced design; subsequent chunk visualizes the selected gene over time.
limitations: The fission source does not identify accession, organism, sample count or package version; these remain open.
No task-specific full/reduced expected results were computed.

title: Interpret Cook's-distance outliers and independent filtering in results

sources.locator: Approach to count outliers; Independent filtering of results; chunks boxplotCooks, filtByMean, noFilt
results details on Cook's-distance flagging and independent filtering

scientific_use: Inspect Cook's distances and determine why result p-values or adjusted p-values are NA; compare default independent filtering with unfiltered results and interpret the chosen mean-normalized-count threshold.
tool_role_basis: The unit uses documented DESeq2 diagnostics and result-extraction options to interpret an existing analysis, without modifying the package implementation.
inputs: Fitted DESeqDataSet and results object from an RNA-seq count analysis.
Optional results arguments cooksCutoff and independentFiltering; target alpha for adjusted-p-value filtering.
outputs: Cook's distance matrix/diagnostic plot; p-values and adjusted p-values where genes are outlier-flagged or below the independent-filter threshold may be NA.
Metadata containing filter threshold and rejections over filter quantiles; optional comparison with independentFiltering=FALSE.
dependencies: DESeq2 fitted objects; sample replication affects outlier behavior (flagging needs at least three replicates; replacement is applied at seven or more replicates under documented defaults).
evidence: Vignette documents Cook's-distance use, replacement/flagging replicate thresholds, and mean-normalized-count filtering optimized for rejection count.
results manual documents NA p-values for Cook's outliers and NA adjusted p-values for genes below the filter threshold.
limitations: The source describes behavior but supplies no labeled gold-standard outlier dataset or mandated biological interpretation.
Thresholds and default behavior are version-sensitive; this record is tied to the pinned source revision.

title: Compare differential-expression methods on simulated negative-binomial counts

sources.locator: simulation grid, meanDispPairs_bottomly load, methods, iCOBRA performance loop

scientific_use: Generate negative-binomial count matrices using mean/dispersion pairs derived from Bottomly data, vary sample count and differential-expression fraction, run DESeq2 and several other methods, and compare FDR/TPR curves against known simulated differential status and fold changes.
tool_role_basis: The benchmark applies existing differential-expression packages but also implements the simulation data-generation procedure in makeSim.R and assembles truth labels and performance comparisons.
inputs: Bottomly-derived mean-dispersion pairs restricted to mean > 10, loaded from meanDispPairs_bottomly.rda.
Simulation grid: 10,000 genes; total samples 6, 8 or 10; differential-expression fraction 0.05, 0.1 or 0.2; random seeds tied to grid index.
Method packages DESeq2, edgeR, DSS, limma/voom, SAMseq, EBSeq and iCOBRA.
outputs: Simulated matrices and known status/logFC truth; iCOBRA FDR-TPR performance plots and saved R objects/package versions.
dependencies: R packages named in the script; sourced makeSim.R and runScripts.R; meanDispPairs_bottomly.rda generated from Bottomly data by code in the false block at the end of testsuite.Rmd.
Script uses parallel::mclapply with two cores and may require substantial memory/runtime; resource sizing is unmeasured.
evidence: icobra_benchmarks.R enumerates method wrappers, simulation parameters, truth variables and FDR/TPR evaluation.
makeSim.R samples Bottomly mean/dispersion pairs and generates negative-binomial counts with known effects.
testsuite.Rmd's disabled code derives dispersion pairs from the Bottomly package dataset; this is adapted empirical parameter reference, not observed task output.
limitations: No simulation or scientific tool was run; reproducibility, runtime and output determinism remain unvalidated.
The required meanDispPairs_bottomly.rda is not listed in the pinned repository tree and must be generated from Bottomly data; exact dataset release and terms are unresolved.
Some scripts inject an EBSeq score from edgeR for plotting; clarify comparator metric semantics before designing a benchmark grader.

title: Shrink log2 fold-change estimates for ranking and visualization

sources.locator: Log fold change shrinkage for visualization and ranking; Alternative shrinkage estimators; chunks lfcShrink and estimator comparison
usage, argument semantics, estimator details and examples

scientific_use: Apply apeglm, ashr or normal-prior shrinkage to fitted coefficient estimates, yielding moderated fold changes and posterior uncertainty useful for gene ranking and MA-plot visualization.
tool_role_basis: The workflow calls DESeq2 lfcShrink and existing apeglm/ashr implementations on fitted results; it applies existing methods rather than implementing shrinkage algorithms.
inputs: DESeqDataSet after DESeq and a coefficient name/number from resultsNames(dds); apeglm requires coef.
Optional lfcThreshold and svalue options alter the inferential target/output; supported estimator and contrast combinations vary.
outputs: DESeqResults with shrunken log2FoldChange and posterior SD stored in lfcSE; prior metadata is accessible through priorInfo.
Vignette compares estimator-specific MA plots for Pasilla treatment effect.
dependencies: DESeq2; apeglm for type=apeglm; ashr for type=ashr; fitted DESeqDataSet with coefficient metadata.
evidence: Vignette calls lfcShrink(dds,coef=condition_treated_vs_untreated,type=apeglm) and shows normal/ashr alternatives.
lfcShrink manual specifies estimator outputs, coefficient requirements, threshold behavior and optional s-values.
limitations: External estimator dependencies, version pins, and license compatibility need checking during authoring.
Source describes ranking/visualization utility but provides no gold-standard rank or task-specific expected posterior values; no execution was performed.
